subject: health
unitTitle: Mental Health Support Systems and Crisis Response
title: Mastery check: reducing stigma through accurate language
essentialQuestion: When self-management is not enough, what is the next step and who takes it with me?
keyPoints: Accurate language describes experiences and support needs without using a condition as an insult or assuming a label; stigma can delay care and isolate people.
Use accurate person-first language, separate a condition or behavior from a person’s worth, and explain how stigma can obstruct information, support, testing, or treatment.
For reducing stigma through accurate language, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Write a peer-support response protocol: what to say, what not to promise, who to bring in, and how to hand off — then draft one short advocacy message for better support access.
studentTask: Review four supplied fictional statements about reducing stigma through accurate language. Label each as accurate, unsupported, or stigmatizing; revise two statements with person-first factual language, and explain how each revision could make information or help-seeking more accessible.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in reducing stigma through accurate language; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the reducing stigma through accurate language task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: The protocol may be written, spoken, or built from supplied response cards that the learner orders and adapts.
extensionChallenge: Apply reducing stigma through accurate language under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.

Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

trustedAdultNote: This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of reducing stigma through accurate language in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
